Seven independent quadrature/reconstruction profiles and boundary checks passed; the proof is analytic and not inferred from finite tests.

The narrow new result is three scalar statistics giving a complete inverse/feasible-set theorem plus cutoff cusp and sharp rectangular inverse sensitivity. This is not a claimed new forward law. Closest published inverse width statistics concern a different observable and sampling protocol. Specialized historical three-feature inversions remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: A natural three-parameter shape class is recovered from three unlabeled scalar data features rather than a whole directional distribution. The complete attainable region gives a practical consistency criterion for ideal chord data; the positive first-cutoff cusp establishes detectability, and the sharp square-root inverse instability explains sensitivity near rectangles. These are structural inverse results and geometric boundaries, not a mere recomputation of a known forward chord formula.
